chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Salamah, and Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn Sayf from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: One prayer in my mosque is equal to one thousand prayers elsewhere.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the Prophet's mosque according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the chain of Ibn Qulawayh, emphasizes the unique spiritual status of the Prophet's Mosque (Masjid al-Nabawi) as a locus of divine grace, where a single prayer yields the reward of a thousand. In Shia scholarly tradition, this multiplicative reward is often interpreted not merely as a numerical increase but as a reflection of the proximity to the Prophet's (s.a.w.) spiritual presence and the intercessory merit associated with his resting place.
